correctness.rationale: Color \(K_{t+2}\) red on a Hamilton cycle and blue off the cycle. For a proposed left pair \(x,y\), an orderable coloring of the whole \(K_{2,t}\) requires one of the two alternating classes \(V_{rb},V_{br}\) to be empty. On a cycle, each of \(x,y\) has a neighbor not shared in the required direction, so both alternating classes are nonempty; hence no orderable spanning \(K_{2,t}\) occurs. With only two colors there is no rainbow triangle, proving both lower bounds. The actual verifier checks all left pairs for \(3\le t\le50\) and directly checks all orderings for the smallest cases. Substitution into the cited upper \(r'_2(K_{2,t})\le CR(K_{2,t},K_3)\le\lfloor4t/3\rfloor+2\) gives 7 and 8 for \(t=4,5\).

value.rationale: The Hamilton-cycle coloring is a uniform explicit obstruction for a natural new Ramsey parameter, and matching it to the best available upper bound settles the first two nontrivial biclique cases beyond the smallest example. The result is modest but mathematically motivated and not just a table lookup.
residual_risks: The all-t lower bound is asymptotically weaker than known constructions.

final_claim: For every \(t\ge3\), the two-color orderable and unordered-canonical biclique Ramsey parameters satisfy \(r'_2(K_{2,t})\ge t+3\) and \(CR(K_{2,t},K_3)\ge t+3\); together with Li’s upper bound this gives the exact values \(r'_2(K_{2,4})=CR(K_{2,4},K_3)=7\) and \(r'_2(K_{2,5})=CR(K_{2,5},K_3)=8\).
limitations: The linear lower bound is not asymptotically sharp compared with the known \(4t/3+o(t)\) scale.
Only \(t=4,5\) are closed exactly by the cited upper bound.
